jobs.prompt:
chore(cpp): integrate the slimming, URL, HTTP client, passkey, BigInt, stored-value and conformance branches onto stage 1 (stage 2b)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s1-c1-44247790145-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). You are an INTEGRATOR (see TASK); keep your own edits to what integration needs.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` that the integration needs. Not `.github/`, not the TypeScript; vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` stay byte-identical to what the branches vendored.

TASK
You start from integration stage 1, `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s1-c1-44247790145-1`: small standard-library helpers, ICU case mapping/collation and llhttp server parsing, already merged and green on ARM64 (443 binaries, 5,037 cases; report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s1-20261118.md`). Merge these reviewed and accepted branches into it with ordinary `git merge` commits, in this order (fetch each from `origin`; each has a report under `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/`: read it before merging):
  1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s1b-20261118-44270540815-1`: four runtime-slimming branches already merged together (console, environment/filesystem, Headers/multipart, ordered containers/gzip).
  2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-llhttp-client-fu-c1-44247790145-1`: fetch response parsing and body framing on llhttp (vendors `third_party/llhttp`, as stage 1 does: must end up as ONE copy, byte-identical).
  3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-ada-c1-44247790145-1`: URL, IDNA and URLSearchParams on ada 4.0.0 (vendors `third_party/ada`).
  4. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-qcbor-c1-44247790145-1`: passkey CBOR on QCBOR 1.6.1 (vendors `third_party/qcbor`; edits the CBOR region at the top of `src/auth/passkeys.cpp`).
  5. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-asn1-c1-44247790145-1`: passkey ASN.1, ECDSA, X.509 and CRL decoding on OpenSSL (edits the lower regions of the SAME file `src/auth/passkeys.cpp`: merge with care, both changes must survive; security-sensitive: no validation may be lost).
  6. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-bigint-c1-44247790145-1`: BigInt on Boost.Multiprecision.
  7. `agent-jobs/cppgw-kv-jsc-graph-model-c1-44247790145-1`: stored-value reader no longer materialises sparse arrays and preserves shared references and cycles.
  8. `agent-jobs/cppgw-conformance-e2e-c1-44247790145-1`: black-box conformance suite (new directory `cpp/gateway/conformance/`, docs).
Expect conflicts in shared registries (`fuzz/targets.json`, `docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tests/LINKS.txt`), in `src/auth/passkeys.cpp` (branches 4 and 5) and where slimming changed a caller another branch also touched. Resolve keeping every branch's intent; never resolve by dropping a branch's change. Then:
  a. Register every vendored library in every build path (CMake, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, the portable CI driver incl. C sources).
  b. Each branch's report lists a few tests it could not touch because they were outside its paths; resolve each under the owner policy, one commit per test with the reason: the WebAuthn replay fixture has non-canonical CBOR vectors that QCBOR's strict wrapper now REJECTS (intended; update those expectations to the rejection, keep every valid vector passing) and 16 warning-text expectations that differ with OpenSSL decoding (wording only: update); `tests/rt/number_test.cpp` expects three incomplete BigInt literals to parse as zero (Bun quirk: update to the library behaviour and record it); fetch tests were already updated by branch 2.
  c. The BigInt and stored-value branches both noted a deep-recursion stack overflow at `-O0` under AddressSanitizer in JSON/array copy paths (passes at `-O1`): confirm the recursion depth is bounded by the 128-level JSON limit / the reader's depth limit in the merged tree and that the driver's `asan` configuration (which uses `-O1`) is clean; if a path can recurse deeper than its documented limit on untrusted input, fix it.
  d. Run the whole suite, release configuration, all shards, then the `asan` configuration for the components these branches touched, then the conformance suite (`cpp/gateway/docs/CONFORMANCE.md`) against the merged native build if Bun 1.4.0 can be installed on your runner; everything must be green on your ARM64 runner.
Write `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s2b-20261118.md`: merge order, each conflict and its resolution, each test decision with justification, final counts per shard, conformance result, first-party production lines in `src/rt` + `src/runtime` + `src/auth/passkeys.cpp` before and after.

DONE WHEN
`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4` passes for N = 1..4 with zero failing binaries on your ARM64 runner, `git log` shows the eight merges, and the report is complete. The maintainer will merge this stage with one more integration branch to produce the final pull request.
